actualFailure.failure: test_32: invalid lock-token recovery created a persistent foreign-token failure marker before authority validation; restoring the correct lock then failed.

rules: The original r2 candidate, its expectations and actual failed receipts remain immutable.
Validate the complete intent, current abandoned-lock token and retained-root digest before dirty becomes true.
Refused authority requests may not create, replace or remove a failure marker and may not modify any source/store/archive bytes.
The abandoned operation lock remains present after a refused request, and successful recovery still requires explicit ownership and plan confirmation.
Repeat all existing checks in _finish immediately before recovery mutation; prevalidation does not waive guards or source closure.
Once actual recovery mutation starts, any failure retains the lock and genuine owner-bound marker; live instance remains poisoned.
A corrected request is accepted only after the caller restores the exact original authority bytes; no automatic repair or deletion of foreign facts is added.

newCases: wrong lock token refusal is byte-preserving and does not poison same-instance legitimate recovery
wrong plan refusal preserves an existing genuine failure marker and later valid recovery
malformed target set refuses before dirty and preserves all persistent bytes
mismatched retained-root digest refuses before dirty and preserves all persistent bytes
failure after actual recovery publication still persists genuine owner guard and requires fresh explicit recovery
